title: 09. Production & Safety: Day 20 — Production-Grade II: Graphs and Streaming RAG
summary: Yesterday we wrapped two agents behind FastAPI. Today we go one layer up: a service whose internal logic is a LangGraph state machine, and a service whose response streams token-by-token to the client instead of arriving as one JSON blob.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
Yesterday we wrapped two agents behind FastAPI. Today we go one layer up: a service whose internal logic is a **LangGraph state machine**, and a service whose response **streams token-by-token** to the client instead of arriving as one JSON blob. Both patterns are common in production agent platforms — graph orchestration for multi-step reasoning, streaming for chat UX.

The graph service shows you how to expose a LangGraph workflow as a typed HTTP endpoint without leaking graph internals to the caller. The streaming service shows you the one FastAPI pattern (`StreamingResponse` with `media_type="text/event-stream"`) that lets browsers render agent output as it is produced.

sections.title: Common Pitfalls
sections.body:
**Chroma in-memory vs persistent.** `chromadb.Client()` is in-process and does not survive restarts. `chromadb.PersistentClient(path=...)` writes to disk. If you forget the `path` argument you silently get an in-memory client and lose everything on restart.

**Streaming but buffering anyway.** If your reverse proxy (nginx, CloudFront) buffers SSE, the client sees the whole response arrive at once. Set `X-Accel-Buffering: no` on the response, or configure `proxy_buffering off` in nginx. Test with `curl -N` from a remote host, not just localhost.

**Storing state in module globals across workers.** The `sessions` dict in Project 2 is per-process. With two uvicorn workers, a user might land on worker A for turn 1 and worker B for turn 2 — losing history. Move session state to Redis or sticky-session your load balancer.

**No recursion limit on the graph.** A LangGraph loop that never terminates will run forever (or until your model budget does). Always pass `config={"recursion_limit": N}` to `ainvoke`, with N small enough to fail fast.

**Mixing `await` and `.invoke()` on streams.** `agent.run_stream(...)` must be used with `async with`. Calling `.stream()` outside the context manager raises a confusing `RuntimeError`. Read the Pydantic AI streaming docs once and stick to the pattern shown above.

**Calling sync Chroma from async code.** `collection.query(...)` is sync. In the example it is fast enough that we tolerate blocking the loop briefly; for larger indexes wrap it with `await asyncio.to_thread(collection.query, ...)`.
